resources.string: Open a photo in Samsung Gallery, then tap the tops of two phones together. No Share button — only a real tap.
Ready — open Gallery and tap phone tops
Samsung blocked Accessibility — do Step 1 first
Step 1 done — now enable TapShare in Accessibility
Samsung blocks Accessibility for sideloaded apps until you allow it.\nTap the button → ⋮ menu (top right) → Allow restricted settings → back.
Installed apps → TapShare → turn ON. If it still says denied, repeat Step 1.
Or pick a photo here, then tap phone tops together.
Allow photos, nearby devices, location, and notifications
Open Gallery → tap phone tops to share

TapShare uses Accessibility only to detect when Samsung Gallery is open and to share the photo on screen when you tap two phones together. It does not read your other apps and does nothing until phones are tapped.
Share Gallery photos by tapping phones together
Find TapShare under Installed apps and turn it ON
In App info tap the ⋮ menu → Allow restricted settings
Tap the tops of both phones together
Both phones must tap tops together. Keep TapShare running on the other phone too.
Both phones: TapShare on, Bluetooth on, Location on, then tap tops firmly together
Open a photo first, then tap
Turn on Bluetooth, then try again
